events.name: Odd One Out
events.intro: A board of six Pokémon silhouettes under glass: a Pikachu, a second Pikachu right beside it, an Eevee, a Snorlax, a Clefairy and a Jigglypuff. A card underneath: **"One of these is an impostor. Which?"** Look closely. One of the two Pikachu has ears that are a little too soft at the tips.

success.text: You tap the glass. The second Pikachu wobbles, sags, and melts into a pink puddle with two dot eyes, deeply embarrassed. It was a Ditto all along, copying the shape beside it. The board clicks open and a little tin of Quick Powder slides out.
You tap the first Pikachu. It stays a Pikachu. Beside it, the second one very quietly lets its ears go a little softer, and you could swear it is relieved.
You tap the Snorlax. Nothing happens. The Snorlax silhouette, to be fair, looks like it would not have moved even if it were the impostor.

events.name: Painting Alignment
events.intro: Four paintings hang crooked in an empty parlour: a Ninetales, a Houndoom, an Arcanine and a Rapidash, each one turned a little away from the cold fireplace. Every one of them looks like it is waiting for a fire.

choices.label: Turn them all to the fireplace.

success.text: You straighten each frame until all four fire Pokémon are looking at the grate together. Something clicks inside the chimney breast, the back of the fireplace swings open, and behind it, in a velvet bag, someone's savings: ₽1,000, and a note that just says "Finally."

choices.label: Turn them all to the window.

success.text: You turn them all to face the window. The room feels colder at once, and nothing opens. Whoever hung them here wanted them looking somewhere else.
You leave the paintings looking where they were looking. They have waited this long.

events.name: Pinball Pokémon Center
events.intro: A giant pinball table in the corner of the Pokémon Center, all chrome and blinking lights, with a Voltorb painted on every bumper. A sign: **"High score 10,000. Beat it, win the prize!"** You notice the left ramp blinks a little brighter than the others.

success.text: You feed in your coins. The table wakes up with a fanfare, the ball drops, and your team crowds round the glass to watch.
You leave the table blinking to itself.

events.name: The Ball Is in Play
events.intro: The ball comes screaming down the middle and you catch it on the flipper. Three ways up: the left ramp, blinking bright, the bumpers in the middle, and the right ramp.

success.text: You send it up the left ramp. BONUS LANE! The whole table lights up, the Voltorb bumpers spin, the score rolls past 10,000 and keeps going. The table plays a tinny fanfare and pays out the prize: a Cell Battery. The left ramp, every time. You will remember that.
You smash it into the bumpers. Bing, bing, bing! It is very exciting and very loud, and when the ball finally drains you have 6,200. Your team cheers anyway.
Up the right ramp and straight back down into the drain. 1,900. The left ramp keeps blinking at you, a little smugly.

events.name: Rune Tiles
events.intro: A sealed stone door with a grid of sliding rune tiles and one empty space. The carving around the frame tells, in pictures, the story of this region's Legendary Pokémon. The runes are letters. Someone meant you to spell something.

choices.label: Slide them to spell the legend's name.

success.text: Tile by tile, you spell out the name of the Pokémon in the carving, in order, the way the old stories say it. The last rune drops into place, and the door breathes out dust that smells like rain. Inside, an offering left long ago, and on the wall, the same shape as the carving, watching you.

effects.text: Spelled the legend's name on a rune door.

success.text: You slide tiles about until your arms ache. The door does not even creak. Somewhere inside it, you get the feeling something is disappointed in you.
You leave the door sealed. It has kept its secret this long.

events.name: Silhouette Quiz
events.intro: **"Who's that Pokémon?!"** A booth with a screen, a buzzer and a host in a sparkly jacket. "Three in a row wins the big prize!" On the screen: a small four-legged shape with something leafy growing out of it. Every child in this region starts with one of three. This is the one that grows.

success.text: BZZT! "It's... CORRECT!" The host throws confetti on you personally. "One for one! Next screen, next booth!"
"Ooh, no! Look at the leaf!" The host is sympathetic. "Still, you can play on. Next booth!"
"Ooh, no! Look at the leaf!" The host pats your shoulder. "Still, play on! Next booth!"

events.name: Silhouette Quiz: Second Shape
events.intro: Booth two. A bigger shadow, broad and proud. The host leans in: "This one has sent a lot of new trainers home crying. The very first Gym Leader of this region trusts it above all others."

success.text: "CORRECT!" More confetti. "You know your Gyms! On to the last booth!"
"Close, but no! Not quite that scary. Not yet." The host points you on to the last booth anyway.
The host laughs so hard they have to sit down. "On you go. Last booth."

events.name: Silhouette Quiz: Final Shape
events.intro: The last booth. The screen shows a shape you know better than any other: the way it stands, the way it tilts its head. It takes a moment, and then your heart catches. It is your own Pokémon, filmed from the crowd.

branches.text: "CORRECT! THREE IN A ROW!" Every light in the place goes off at once, the host is crying a bit, and you are handed the big prize: a Rare Candy, in a little velvet box. "You'd know them anywhere, wouldn't you?" Your Pokémon is very pleased to have been on television.

success.text: "CORRECT!" The host beams. "Of course you knew. You'd know them anywhere." Your Pokémon is very pleased to have been on television.
"A Ditto?" The host looks at the screen, then at your Pokémon. "Oh, that's cold." Your lead looks up at you, wounded.
"A Zorua? No! It's your own Pokémon!" Your lead stares at you. You will be making this up to it for a while.

events.name: Slide Whistle Safe
events.intro: A safe in the corner of a ruined house, with no dial, only a slide whistle hanging on a string from the handle. Scratched into the paint: three little lines, one short, one middle, one tall.

success.text: You blow a low note. Something inside the safe clunks, once, as if agreeing. Two more notes to go.
You blow a middle note. The safe stays silent. You try to go on anyway.
You blow a high note. Somewhere upstairs a Whismur starts howling along. The safe stays shut. You try to go on.

events.name: The Second Note
events.intro: The safe waits. The three scratches are still there: short, middle, tall.

success.text: Low again. The safe does nothing. One more note.
A middle note. Clunk. Two clunks now. One more.
A high note. Silence. One more.

events.name: The Last Note
events.intro: One note left. Your team holds its breath.

success.text: Low. Nothing. The safe stays shut, and the slide whistle sounds a little sad.
Middle. Nothing. You put the whistle down.

branches.text: Low, middle, high. CLUNK. The safe door swings open on a velvet tray, and on it, a Metronome, ticking gently as if it had been keeping time for you all along.

success.text: High. Nothing happens. Low, middle, high: you were close.

events.name: Echo Cave Sonar Puzzle
events.intro: Pitch black. Somewhere ahead, pings echo off the walls: one loud, bouncing back hard, and one soft, almost swallowed. A trickle of air from somewhere says there is a way through.

success.text: You follow the loud ping straight into a wall. Of course: a wall is what sends a ping back loud. You feel your way back out, a bit bruised in your pride.

The soft ping is the one the dark swallows, so that is where the gap is. You follow it through, and on the far side, in the first grey light, something glints: a Wide Lens, dropped by someone who did not find the way.
Your Zubat is gone in a flicker and back in a moment, chirping smugly, and leads you straight through the dark as if it were noon. On the far side, a Wide Lens is lying in the grey light.

events.name: Speed Typing Terminal
events.intro: An old terminal in a closed-down office blinks: **TYPE THE LINE BEFORE THE TIMER ENDS.** Below it, the line: *"I'll be the very best."*

success.text: You type it with two fingers, then all of them, and hit the last key with a second to spare. The terminal plays a little tune, and a drawer pops open. Inside, a TM, and a sticky note: "Like no one ever was."

events.name: Star Chart
events.intro: A planetarium dome, dark and quiet. A star chart is painted on the floor with a dozen loose stars you can drag about. In the middle, one empty shape: round, with two pointed ears and a curl.

branches.text: You know this one now. The stars fall into the Clefairy shape under your hands almost by themselves, and the dome lights up again, just for you.

success.text: You drag the stars into the shape of a Clefairy, the one the old charts call the Moon Pixie, and the dome lights up overhead with the real sky. A hatch in the floor slides open on a little gift.
You make a very good Pidgey. Nothing happens. The empty shape in the middle still has two pointed ears and a curl.
You leave the stars where they lie.

events.name: Tide Gauge
events.intro: A lock gate on a canal, and a big brass dial. The water on your side is too high; the plaque says the gate opens only when the water is exactly level. Three levers: raise, lower, hold. The gauge looks like it overshoots.

success.text: The water drains with a gurgle. Lower, but not level yet.
The water rises the wrong way, sloshing over your boots. You keep trying.
You hold. Nothing changes, and the gate stays shut. You keep trying.

events.name: Still Not Level
events.intro: The dial wavers. Not level yet.

success.text: Lower again: too far now, the needle dips under the line. One more pull.
Up it goes. The needle swings past. One more pull.
You hold, and nothing changes. One more pull.

events.name: The Last Lever
events.intro: One more pull, and then the gate decides.

branches.text: Lower, lower, then raise just a little. The needle settles dead on the line, the gate swings open, and the canal carries you through the sea lock, well past a stretch of open water.

success.text: Up a little. The needle swings and settles off the line. The gate stays shut.
Lower. The gate stays shut, the water too low now.
You hold. The gate stays shut.

events.name: Tilt Maze
events.intro: An Electrode sits at the start of a wooden maze on a table, looking smug. A sign: **"Roll it to the goal. Do not rest it on a corner."** The Electrode looks at the corners with interest.

success.text: You tilt it slow and steady, always along a wall, never letting it settle in a corner. It rolls into the goal and sparks with delight, and the table drawer pops open on an Electric Gem.

You tilt it fast and it rolls into a corner and stops. There is a pause. BOOM. A small, harmless, very loud explosion, and the Electrode is back at the start, looking even more smug. Your hair will be standing up for an hour.

events.name: Weighted Scales
events.intro: Four identical gems and a balance scale on a table. **"One is real and heavier. Find it in only two weighs."**

success.text: Two on each side. The left side sinks: the real one is one of those two.
One against one. They balance. Two gems left you have not tried, and only one weigh to go.

events.name: The Second Weigh
events.intro: One weigh left.

branches.text: The two from the heavier side, one against one. One side sinks, and there it is. As you lift it, the real gem catches the light and turns out to be a Shiny Stone.

success.text: One against one. They balance, and you have to guess between the last two. You guess wrong; the gem goes cloudy in your hand.
Two against two again. The scale tips the same way as before, and tells you nothing new. You are out of weighs.

events.name: The Express Train
events.intro: A little train stops at a halt in the middle of nowhere. The conductor grins down at you: "Express! Skips a stop! Ticket is free if you can answer this: which is the baby, Pikachu or Pichu?"

success.text: "Correct! Hop on, free of charge!" The train whistles, your team crowds the window, and a whole stop goes by in a blur.
"Oh, dear. That's the grown-up!" The conductor shakes their head, still smiling. "₽100, then." You pay, and the train whistles you past a whole stop anyway.

events.name: The Looping Forest
events.intro: Every path out of this clearing leads back into it. A carving on a stump says: **"Walk only where the mushrooms glow."**

success.text: You walk only where the little mushrooms glow, step after step. The trees thin, the light changes, and you are out, with a Tiny Mushroom in your pocket that one of your Pokémon picked on the way.
You mark every tree you pass with a scratch, and very soon every tree you pass already has your scratch on it. You are back in the clearing.

events.name: The Old Lab Terminal
events.intro: An abandoned lab. One terminal still glows: **"PASSWORD: the next number. 3, 6, 12, 24, ?"**

success.text: ACCESS GRANTED. A door at the back hisses open on a small room with a single case in it, and in the case, an Up-Grade, still humming.
ACCESS DENIED. An alarm wails, and a Magnemite floats out of the wall to deal with you.
You leave the terminal glowing.

events.name: The Mirror Maze
events.intro: A maze of mirrors, and in every one of them, you. Your team bumps noses with its own reflections. One reflection, a long way down, does not quite move when you move.

success.text: You keep one hand on the glass and walk. It takes a long, long time, and you see far too much of your own face, but eventually the glass ends and you are outside, blinking.

choices.label: Follow the reflection that doesn't copy you.

success.text: You walk toward the one reflection that will not copy you, and it turns out not to be a reflection at all: it is a window, and on the other side is the way out. On the sill, someone has left a pinch of Bright Powder in a twist of paper.

events.name: The Plate Room
events.intro: Three stone plates: a sun, a moon and a star. A mural over them shows the sky through one night: the sun goes down, the moon comes up, and then the star comes out.

success.text: The sun plate sinks with a grinding sound: the sun goes down first. Two plates left.
The moon plate does not budge, and a little dart of dust puffs out of the wall at you. The night does not start with the moon.
The star plate does not budge. Dust puffs out of the wall. Not yet.

events.name: The Plate Room: Second Plate
events.intro: The sun plate is down. Two plates left: the moon and the star.

success.text: The moon rises next. The plate sinks, and the star plate begins to glow.
The star plate stays still. Dust puffs out of the wall. The moon comes first.

events.name: The Plate Room: Last Plate
events.intro: Only the star is left, glowing faintly.

success.text: The star plate sinks, and the whole wall grinds open. In the alcove behind it, where the mural's night sky ends, a Comet Shard is lying in the dust, glittering.

effects.text: Walked the night across three plates.

events.name: The Portal Switches
events.intro: Three switches and a dead portal, all cobwebs and quiet. A plaque: **"Sky before sea, and sea before stone."**

success.text: Sky, then sea, then stone. The portal shudders, crackles and opens on a swirl of light. You step through with your team holding on to you, and step out two whole stops further down the road.
The portal coughs out a puff of dust and a single forgotten Poké Ball. That is all it does.
The portal flickers and spits out a very confused Porygon, which takes it personally.

events.name: The Riddle Signpost
events.intro: A signpost with no place names, only a riddle: **"The more of me you take, the more you leave behind. Answer, and the short way opens."**

success.text: The signpost creaks around on its pole to point down a path you had not seen. The short way. You take it, and leave a great many footsteps behind.
A good answer, but the signpost does not move. Time, it seems, is not what it had in mind.
You say it quietly. The signpost does not move, but you think about it for a long while as you walk on.

events.name: The Sundial Ruins
events.intro: An old sundial in the ruins, its arm loose. Carved round it: **"Turn me to where my shadow is shortest, and I will open."**

success.text: At noon the sun stands highest and the shadow is shortest. You turn the arm, the stone base splits along a seam, and inside, warm to the touch, a Sun Stone.
You turn it to the north. Nothing happens. A shadow is shortest at a time, not a place.
You turn it to the east, toward the dawn. Nothing. At dawn the shadows are long.
